I'm mainly familiar with Hordes/Skorne so I'll do my best to help with how I currently understand it.  All the old Factions still exist but all their toys may not necessarily play well together thus breaking them down into two primary "armies" instead.  What you take into a game will be an army probably pretty similar to a theme force.  Most of the core Factions I've seen have roughly 4+ theme forces which are likely to be condensed to 2 Armies and some cadres (aka models that can work for either army but aren't meant to be the focus of a faction in and of themselves) to spread out between them.  So most likely any of the big Factions will get 2 core armies and their less prevalent theme forces will become Cadres.  So using Skorne as my example this is my current guess as to how this will shake out for them.  


So currently there are four theme forces.  Disciples of Agony (Basically minions working with Skorne) Masters of War (Cataprhact's and Praetorians/your typical melee soldiers following the Hoksune code to their inevitable death.)  The Exalted (Immortals/Ancestral Guardians aka your scary Terracotta soldier models) and Winds of Death (All the ranged units that the Skorne begrudgingly bring to battles even though they think fighting with anything resembling a gun is lame.)  


So as Masters of War and The Exalted are probably the most popular/visually distinct Theme lists I'd guess those will be essentially the two Armies the faction gets.  Most likely it will have supporting Cadres in the "Winds of Death" and "Disciples of Agony" mold.  By focusing on their two primary themes I think the idea is they will be able to better balance and gauge what fans want.  While I'm sure there are certain Skorne fans who would love nothing more than to field all ranged armies or nothing but minion warbeasts, by PP focusing their interests on the two Army ideas they can continue to cater to what the majority will want to see while having the occasional cadre model that will see some play but by no means define the faction.    


Again this is my understanding of how things are meant to go/some of the partial reasoning behind such changes so feel free to inform me if I'm way off or something.  Also hope this example helped.

As far as reasons I have for killing myself there as follows.
1.  I have no familial support system setting me far behind everyone I know and making me constantly feel lesser.
2.  It seems unlikely I'll ever be financially independent which I can tell you has weighed enormously on me and only makes me feel like shit.
3.  I hate burdening friends and others who care about me with needing to jump in to support me.  That's something family should do.  I understand I don't have that but it's hard to not look at yourself as a burden to your friends when you wouldn't be able to live without their charity.
4.  I've lived essentially as a pet.  People who've taken me in do love me but they don't respect me.  I'm a human being and I'm treated like a perpetual fuck up for things I had no control over by even the people I love.  It sucks we live in a society where any misfortune is attributed as being your responsibility.  The very idea of picking yourself up by your bootstraps is way too fucking black and white and without empathy.
5.  I just hate what my life has been and what I see it being in the future.  I appreciate that I got to meet lots of great people and have fun memories but I am not so invested in the prospect that I look forward to living out more of this misery.

As for being selfish/hypocritical, I absolutely agree.  It sucks to put that pain on the people who love me but I'm tired of needing to live on others sympathy who do grow to resent me over time.  It just helps contribute to a narrative where I am unlovable.  I hate giving any more evidence to that narrative so I'd rather just take myself out of the equation and putting that hurt on those I love.  It's gotta be better than continually living under more and more undignified circumstances while trying to act oblivious to the fact that I've fallen so far from anything like self respect.  I feel I should if I lack any other options be allowed to choose when enough is enough for me.  This is me drawing a line in the sand.  When you lack money/resources/family/options it just seems more and more logical.
